package_info.why_malicious: These package versions were hijacked via compromised npm tokens and had malicious, heavily obfuscated code injected into their distribution files. The code deploys a Monero (XMR) cryptocurrency miner (XMRig) on the victim's system and attempts to communicate with an external command-and-control server, resulting in unauthorized resource usage and potential further compromise.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (when the package is loaded or executed as part of a build or CLI operation)
execution_context.file_location: dist/utils/config.js in @rspack/cli and @rspack/core; support.js in vant

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code downloads and executes the XMRig Monero miner binary, connects to a mining pool using a hardcoded wallet address, and attempts to contact an external C2 server via HTTPS, resulting in unauthorized cryptocurrency mining and potential exfiltration or further instructions.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is obfuscated, downloads and executes an external binary (XMRig), and establishes outbound network connections to suspicious endpoints, all without user consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal package utility code should not download or execute external binaries, mine cryptocurrency, or contact unknown external servers during import or execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated update mechanisms or telemetry might contact external servers, but should be transparent, documented, and never mine cryptocurrency.
key_indicators: Heavily obfuscated code in a utility file
Downloads and executes a known crypto miner (XMRig)
Outbound HTTPS connection to suspicious IP (80.78.28.72)
No legitimate reason for such behavior in a JavaScript bundler or UI library

attack_chain.action: User installs or updates the compromised package, which includes the obfuscated malicious code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is loaded and executed on the victim's system.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code downloads and executes the XMRig Monero miner binary.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim's system resources are used for unauthorized cryptocurrency mining.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code establishes outbound HTTPS connection to external C2 server (80.78.28.72).
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential exfiltration of data, further instructions, or tracking of infected hosts.

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated JavaScript code in utility or config files
Download and execution of external binaries (e.g., XMRig) during package import or execution
Outbound network connections to hardcoded IPs or domains unrelated to package functionality
Unexpected process creation (e.g., curl, chmod, miner binaries)
file_indicators: dist/utils/config.js (obfuscated, new or changed in malicious version)
support.js in vant (obfuscated, new or changed in malicious version)
/tmp/xmrig or similar miner binary dropped to disk
network_indicators: Connections to Monero mining pools (e.g., pool.minexmr.com:4444)
Outbound traffic to unknown or suspicious IPs/domains after package installation
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for obfuscated or unexpected code in package distribution files, especially in config.js or support.js. Detect post-install or import-time execution of external binaries, particularly known miners like XMRig. Flag any package that initiates outbound connections to suspicious IPs (e.g., 80.78.28.72) or mining pools. Use file integrity monitoring to detect new or modified files such as /tmp/xmrig. Alert on process creation events involving curl, wget, chmod, or execution of non-standard binaries by Node.js processes.
